title: The Big Timeline
concept: Chronology, dating clues and anachronism
enquiry: How can clues help us place local events in a defensible chronological order?
current_ticket: My clue; my claim about when it belongs; a limitation; what I want to investigate next.
elicited: Ordered events, one dating clue, a century/range decision and any uncertainty.
interpret: Distinguish secure chronology from a century misconception, an access barrier or weak clue use.
bounded_voice: Choose a locally relevant approved period or event for the next source set; a neutral local/general route must be available instead of family disclosure.
audience: A named adult or peer restates the event, the clue and the uncertainty before responding.
influence: The teacher selects or foregrounds an approved source from the chosen period and reports that choice at the next arrival.
next_step: Secure: unfamiliar event. Mixed: contrast two clues. Misconception: re-model century/range. Access: physical timeline or oral/scribed route.
tutor: BUILD lesson closure remains adult-received. Tutor time may collate the existing sheet only after subject approval; no extra closure line.
boundary: Do not treat a corridor display as Audience by itself. Do not require family history disclosure.
award: Map only to the exact selected UAS outcome and required evidence; the ticket alone is not unit completion.

title: History Detectives
concept: Source content, inference and limits
enquiry: How can we distinguish what a source shows from what we infer or still cannot know?
current_ticket: The source shows; I infer; I still cannot know; the source type I trust or question.
elicited: A source observation, an inference tied to a detail and an explicit limit.
interpret: Read whether the pupil separates source content from inference and whether the limit is question-specific.
bounded_voice: Choose which approved source type should be added to answer the unresolved question.
audience: Receiver uses the three-part restatement: 'You noticed… you inferred… you still cannot know…'.
influence: The next lesson includes the chosen approved source type or the teacher explains why another source was needed.
next_step: Secure: corroborating source. Mixed: compare observation vs inference. Misconception: re-model 'source is evidence for a question'. Access: enlarged/audio/transcribed source.
tutor: Existing item may be selected and captioned in exact pupil words only after subject approval; no retrospective inference is written by a tutor.
boundary: Constructed sources must be visibly labelled; provenance and rights must be available.
award: Offer candidate evidence only where the exact UAS outcome accepts this method and the source pack is approved.

title: Why People Came
concept: Multi-causality
enquiry: How can several causes combine to influence migration to the Tees Valley?
current_ticket: Two causes; the cause I think mattered most; because.
elicited: At least two causes and a reasoned weighting.
interpret: Check whether the pupil explains combination rather than lists causes or assumes the nearest event is most important.
bounded_voice: Choose which approved person/community case should illustrate the strongest causal chain next.
audience: Adult receives the causal chain and asks only for the link between cause and outcome.
influence: The selected approved case becomes a worked example or comparison in Week 4, with report-back.
next_step: Secure: counterfactual. Mixed: connect two causes. Misconception: model condition/trigger. Access: cause cards and oral chain.
tutor: Collate the existing chain/photo; no tutor-generated 'because' clause.
boundary: Preference does not decide historical importance; evidence and criteria remain non-negotiable.
award: Exact UAS outcome/evidence method required before filing as candidate evidence.

title: People Who Shaped Britain
concept: Agency, context and avoiding a single story
enquiry: How can evidence show why a person or community matters without reducing them to one story?
current_ticket: Person/community; why they matter; evidence; how I avoided reducing them.
elicited: An evidence-based agency claim plus contextual complexity.
interpret: Check whether the claim is evidenced, whether context is present and whether a group is stereotyped.
bounded_voice: Nominate from an approved evidence set and state the criterion, not popularity alone.
audience: A peer or adult restates claim, evidence and the avoided simplification.
influence: Evidence-led nominations shape the comparison set for significance in Week 5.
next_step: Secure: add context/counterevidence. Mixed: evidence-to-claim link. Misconception: re-model agency vs fame. Access: visual evidence grid.
tutor: Existing nomination/evidence may be filed; no new biography or stereotype correction is authored in tutor time.
boundary: Use respectful, plural accounts; no pupil is required to represent a community.
award: Unit alignment must be exact; nomination/vote alone is not evidence of an outcome.

title: Big Deal or Small Deal?
concept: Historical significance by criteria
enquiry: How can we judge significance using criteria rather than fame or personal liking?
current_ticket: Big/small deal; affected whom; for how long; what changed; possible disagreement.
elicited: A significance judgement using impact, reach, duration or remembrance and a challenge.
interpret: Distinguish criterion-based significance from fame, liking or presentism.
bounded_voice: Choose the criterion to foreground and explain why it fits the enquiry.
audience: Receiver restates judgement, criterion and disagreement before commenting.
influence: Judgements set the focus and argument offered in the Week 6 storyboard.
next_step: Secure: change timescale/perspective. Mixed: compare criteria. Misconception: model significance is question-dependent. Access: criteria cards.
tutor: One existing significance item may be collated; no new judgement is supplied.
boundary: Do not rank pupils or communities; challenge ideas with evidence.
award: A criterion-based judgement may be candidate evidence only against the exact outcome.

title: Plan the Story
concept: Sequence, evidence and explanation in an account
enquiry: How can sequence, evidence and explanation turn facts into a coherent account?
current_ticket: First/then; key evidence; explanation linking them.
elicited: A sequence controlled by a claim, evidence selection and an explanatory link.
interpret: Check whether the plan is a list, a story without evidence or a coherent historical account.
bounded_voice: Choose communication mode and audience from viable options; name the support that preserves authorship.
audience: Teacher/TA reads back the planned claim and sequence without improving it.
influence: Communication preferences and gaps determine the Week 7 route and approved support.
next_step: Secure: transfer to another event. Mixed: add link. Misconception: re-model chronology vs causation. Access: storyboard/scribe/exact read-back.
tutor: May organise existing pages in order; must not improve the plan or add content.
boundary: Support and authorship must be distinguishable.
award: The plan is curriculum work unless the exact UAS outcome recognises it.

title: Tell the Story
concept: Communicating an evidential account to an audience
enquiry: How can I communicate a historical account so an audience understands claim, evidence and uncertainty?
current_ticket: Mode used; what the audience received; what they questioned or valued.
elicited: A communicated account plus evidence of audience reception and one response.
interpret: Check whether the audience understood the claim/evidence, not merely whether a presentation occurred.
bounded_voice: Choose speaking, writing, drawing or recording and consent to any display.
audience: Named person listens/reads and restates claim, evidence and uncertainty.
influence: Audience responses and recommendations shape Week 8 map emphasis and future provision.
next_step: Secure: adapt for another audience. Mixed: clarify claim. Misconception: separate fact and inference. Access: alternative mode.
tutor: May collate a subject-approved recording, image or sheet; no audience is invented retrospectively.
boundary: Use representative work, not 'best work'; obtain consent and avoid face capture where unnecessary.
award: Performance evidence needs exact outcome mapping and authentic reception evidence.

title: Where in the World?
concept: Mapping migration, spatial connection and curriculum influence
enquiry: How does mapping movement change our understanding of migration, connection and identity?
current_ticket: Route mapped; recommendation; named adult; report-back date.
elicited: A mapped route, one geographical/historical insight and a bounded recommendation.
interpret: Check map accuracy, what geography adds and whether the recommendation is actionable.
bounded_voice: Choose one resource/curriculum/cultural recommendation within the decision-maker's power.
audience: Named adult with authority receives the recommendation and its evidence.
influence: Adult acts or explains why not, with a report-back date.
next_step: Secure: change scale or compare route. Mixed: re-read map. Method problem: repair grid/scale. Access: enlarged tactile/colour-safe map.
tutor: May help collate the approved map and recommendation; report-back is not a pupil assessment tally.
boundary: Map licence and credits required. No promise should be offered unless an adult can act.
award: Map/recommendation evidence must match the exact UAS outcome; report-back is participation evidence, not automatic award evidence.

title: Time Detectives
concept: Chronology, intervals and challenging a timeline
enquiry: How can dates, periods and intervals help us build and challenge chronology?
current_ticket: Chronology claim; because; what would increase certainty; challenge.
elicited: A defensible ordering, interval reasoning and a challenge/uncertainty.
interpret: Read whether the pupil uses chronological evidence rather than surface familiarity.
bounded_voice: Choose which approved chronology puzzle or period needs further source support.
audience: Peer restates claim, evidence and uncertainty; adult listens for the historical move.
influence: Misconceptions/questions set Week 2 date supports and source set.
next_step: Secure: unfamiliar chronology. Mixed: contrast intervals. Misconception: re-model century/period. Access: physical line.
tutor: Optional pupil re-read of the existing written close; no adult initial and no new next step.
boundary: No catch-up debt if tutor slot missed.
award: Exact UAS mapping required.

title: Source Detectives
concept: Provenance, content, context and source limits
enquiry: How do provenance, content and context affect what a source tells, suggests or cannot prove?
current_ticket: Provenance; strong for; weak for; cannot prove.
elicited: Question-specific evaluation of a source's evidential value.
interpret: Check for 'biased therefore useless', generic reliability language or unsupported inference.
bounded_voice: Choose the unanswered question and the type of corroborating source from an approved pack.
audience: Receiver restates enquiry, source detail, strength and limit.
influence: Source challenges determine corroboration and causal claims in Week 3.
next_step: Secure: conflicting source. Mixed: strength/limit comparison. Misconception: source-as-evidence for a question. Access: transcript/audio/crop.
tutor: Read existing line beside work/next step only; no source evaluation added by tutor.
boundary: Provenance label and constructed-source status mandatory.
award: Candidate evidence only if the exact outcome accepts the evidence form.

title: Cause and Consequence
concept: Motives, conditions, triggers and causal weighting
enquiry: How do personal motives, wider conditions and triggers combine to cause migration?
current_ticket: Motive; condition; trigger; highest-ranked cause; because.
elicited: A causal chain and weighted verdict using a counterfactual or comparison.
interpret: Check whether the pupil confuses chronology with cause, lists rather than links, or overweights the trigger.
bounded_voice: Choose from approved cases which person/community enters the Week 4 agency case study, justified by the causal evidence.
audience: Challenger may probe only the link/evidence; receiver restates the chain before challenge.
influence: Evidence-led selection shapes the next case study, with next-arrival report-back.
next_step: Secure: comparison/counterfactual. Mixed: connect cause types. Misconception: re-model condition/motive/trigger. Access: chain cards.
tutor: Optional re-read; existing causal chain may be collated after teacher approval. No tutor-written causal link.
boundary: A ballot without evidence is not historical assessment or meaningful influence.
award: Exact outcome mapping required.

title: People Who Shaped Britain
concept: Agency within context
enquiry: How can we explain historical agency while recognising context and evidence?
current_ticket: Person/community; change; enabling context; evidence.
elicited: An agency claim balanced with structural/contextual factors.
interpret: Check hero-story simplification, unsupported agency or context that erases action.
bounded_voice: Evidence-led nomination from approved sources, with a named criterion.
audience: Peer validates reasoning, not popularity; restates claim/evidence/context.
influence: Nominations set the Week 5 comparison set.
next_step: Secure: counterexample. Mixed: add context. Misconception: agency vs structure. Access: dual-column organiser.
tutor: May file existing evidence; no new biographical claims.
boundary: No pupil represents a whole community; use plural histories.
award: Exact UAS outcome/evidence required.

title: How Big a Deal?
concept: Significance by criteria, perspective and timescale
enquiry: How can criteria, perspective and timescale produce a defensible significance judgement?
current_ticket: Degree; significant to whom; timescale; criterion; challenge; defend/revise.
elicited: A qualified significance judgement that can be revised.
interpret: Check criterion use, perspective, timescale and response to challenge.
bounded_voice: Choose the criterion/perspective to test and the support request for account planning.
audience: Partner restates judgement and criterion before challenge.
influence: Judgements and support requests shape Week 6 questions, source pairings and access.
next_step: Secure: new perspective/timescale. Mixed: compare criteria. Misconception: significance is constructed. Access: criteria matrix.
tutor: Optional re-read; no new criterion or verdict.
boundary: Disagreement is historical reasoning, not pupil failure.
award: Candidate evidence only after exact mapping.

title: Plan the Account
concept: Planning chronology, causation and source evidence
enquiry: How can a plan organise chronology, causation and source evidence into an account?
current_ticket: Main claim; order; key source evidence; agreed support.
elicited: A controlling claim, planned sequence, evidence allocation and access contract.
interpret: Check whether support preserves authorship and whether each paragraph serves the claim.
bounded_voice: Choose approved access/communication route and identify what support should be present.
audience: Teacher reads back the plan and agreed support; no content is added.
influence: The plan and access contract set Week 7 assessment conditions.
next_step: Secure: stress-test thesis. Mixed: paragraph-to-claim link. Misconception: evidence dump. Access: read-back/scribe/exact record.
tutor: May help organise existing sealed materials but must not alter plan or issue a new next step.
boundary: Assessment support decisions are centre-controlled; access is never withheld by tier.
award: Planning evidence is not the assessed outcome unless exact UAS outcome says so.

title: Write the Account ★ assessed
concept: Independent evidential account under supervised conditions
enquiry: How can I construct an independent account that uses evidence, explanation and qualified uncertainty?
current_ticket: Assessment reflection on claim, evidence, explanation, uncertainty and access used.
elicited: The assessed account itself and a separate post-pens-down conditions reflection.
interpret: Authorised assessor interprets the account; Lundy response concerns conditions only, not answer content during assessment.
bounded_voice: Choose station/access within approved conditions and give post-assessment feedback on conditions.
audience: Real assessor marks/returns. Any anthology uses a representative consented range, not 'best' only.
influence: Conditions feedback informs Week 8 and future assessment; report back what changed or why not.
next_step: Teacher gives one next step after assessment review. Tutor does not edit, annotate or improve the assessed work.
tutor: No curation or upload until the subject teacher confirms the assessment is complete and the normal evidence route is authorised.
boundary: Protected file. No overlay may change task, timing, scaffolds, answer, conditions or access wording.
award: UAS claim only through exact registered unit/outcomes and centre process; AO language is developmental, not a grade.

title: Where in the World?
concept: Atlas evidence, spatial scale and assessment-informed reteaching
enquiry: How can atlas evidence and spatial scale deepen—but not replace—historical explanation?
current_ticket: Routes; what geography adds; recommendation; adult owner/report-back.
elicited: Accurate mapping plus explanation of what spatial evidence adds/does not settle.
interpret: Check map method, scale reasoning and whether geography is being used as a substitute for history.
bounded_voice: Choose an evidence-led curriculum/resource recommendation within adult power.
audience: Named adult receives evidence and recommendation.
influence: Adult action/reasoned response reported back.
next_step: Secure: change scale. Mixed: compare map/evidence. Method: repair map. Access: map alternative.
tutor: May collate approved map after normal subject review; no backlog if not ready.
boundary: OS/map rights and source credits required.
award: Exact UAS mapping required.

title: Source Investigation
concept: How far sources support a claim
enquiry: How far does a source support a claim?
current_ticket: Degree of support; provenance/context limit; weighed judgement.
elicited: Claim-specific use of content, provenance, context, corroboration and weighting.
interpret: Check whether evidence is cited, limits are weighted and the verdict answers 'how far'.
bounded_voice: Choose the next approved causation claim/docket after defending which unresolved issue matters.
audience: Class 'bench' probes cited details only and restates claim, evidence and limit.
influence: The selected docket shapes Week 2, with report-back. Selection is bounded by curriculum and source availability.
next_step: Secure: same sources/new claim. Mixed: evidence-to-verdict. Misconception: bias/utility. Access: source chunking/audio.
tutor: Optional re-read of existing close; staff-only warrant specimen may be observed, but no new pupil wording ships.
boundary: 'Best verdicts' should become a representative consented range. Approved provenance required.
award: AO3 bridge is developmental; exact UAS outcome required.

title: Cause & Consequence Courtroom
concept: Decisive, contributing and background causes
enquiry: Which causes were decisive, contributing or background?
current_ticket: Cause categories; verdict; because.
elicited: Causal classification, weighting, counterargument and verdict.
interpret: Check causal mechanisms and whether labels are justified.
bounded_voice: Choose the appeal question or approved archive issue for Week 3.
audience: Courtroom receiver restates causal chain and evidence before challenge.
influence: Appeal question selects Week 3 archive source within approved pack.
next_step: Secure: counterfactual/appeal. Mixed: mechanism. Misconception: temporal proximity. Access: role cards/visual chain.
tutor: Existing item only; no new verdict or appeal authored.
boundary: Courtroom performance must not reward confidence over reasoning.
award: Exact outcome mapping required.

title: Archive: Nature, Origin & Purpose
concept: Question-specific source utility
enquiry: What is the source genuinely useful for?
current_ticket: Nature/origin/purpose; useful for; not useful for; why it counts for this enquiry.
elicited: Contextualised utility judgement with a question-specific yield and limit.
interpret: Check generic NOP formula, provenance without content or blanket rejection.
bounded_voice: Choose which evidence should be admitted to the turning-point enquiry from an approved set.
audience: Receiver restates enquiry, yield, bar and limitation.
influence: Utility decisions control Week 4 evidence set; teacher reports what was admitted and why.
next_step: Secure: complementary source. Mixed: content+provenance. Misconception: purpose equals unreliability. Access: NOP cards.
tutor: Existing utility item only, after subject approval.
boundary: Source provenance/constructed label mandatory.
award: Developmental AO3; exact UAS mapping.

title: A Century of Change
concept: Change, continuity and turning points
enquiry: How far was the period a turning point?
current_ticket: Change; continuity; degree of turning point; strongest evidence.
elicited: A periodised judgement balancing change and continuity.
interpret: Check presentism, single-event turning point and timescale control.
bounded_voice: Choose the continuity or change problem that should frame the Week 5 agency debate.
audience: Peer restates judgement, evidence and timescale before counter.
influence: Selected problem opens Week 5 debate.
next_step: Secure: alternative timescale. Mixed: change/continuity balance. Misconception: change means total replacement. Access: timeline comparison.
tutor: Existing item only; no new turning-point conclusion.
boundary: Ensure substantive knowledge is secure before analytic demand.
award: Exact UAS mapping required.

title: People & Modern Britain
concept: Agency versus structure
enquiry: How far did individuals shape modern Britain?
current_ticket: Individual; agency; structural conditions; defended judgement and counter.
elicited: A balanced agency/structure judgement with counterargument.
interpret: Check great-person narrative, structural determinism and evidence balance.
bounded_voice: Choose the defended judgement that becomes a Week 6 thesis option, from approved evidence.
audience: Receiver restates judgement, evidence, structure and counter.
influence: Defended judgement becomes thesis choice.
next_step: Secure: counter-case. Mixed: add structure/counter. Misconception: agency as fame. Access: evidence matrix.
tutor: Existing item only.
boundary: Plural representation and no forced identity disclosure.
award: Exact UAS mapping required.

title: Structured Account
concept: Thesis-controlled sustained argument
enquiry: How can a thesis control a sustained argument?
current_ticket: Thesis; paragraph order; strongest evidence; agreed support.
elicited: A thesis, argument architecture, evidence allocation and access contract.
interpret: Check whether paragraphs serve thesis and whether support preserves authorship.
bounded_voice: Choose thesis from viable taught options and agree access conditions.
audience: Teacher reads back thesis/plan and conditions without improving content.
influence: Plan and access contract set Week 7 assessment.
next_step: Secure: stress-test counter. Mixed: paragraph function. Misconception: topic list vs thesis. Access: planning format.
tutor: No alteration of the sealed plan; normal storage only.
boundary: Protected assessment preparation.
award: Plan does not equal assessed outcome unless exact UAS unit says so.

title: Source Assessment ★ assessed
concept: Assessed source utility and substantiated judgement
enquiry: How useful are the sources for the enquiry?
current_ticket: Most/least useful; why; substantiated judgement; access used.
elicited: The assessed source answer and post-assessment conditions feedback.
interpret: Authorised assessor evaluates answer; participation feedback concerns conditions only.
bounded_voice: Choose station/access within approved conditions and one post-assessment design recommendation.
audience: Real assessor; any anthology uses a representative consented range rather than only top answers.
influence: Post-assessment condition recommendation is considered and reported back.
next_step: Teacher gives one next step after marking; tutor does not alter assessed work.
tutor: No upload/caption/edit until subject teacher authorises the normal route after assessment completion.
boundary: Protected file. No content support during assessment. No post-hoc audience or answer enhancement.
award: UAS exact unit/outcomes/process; AO3 developmental, not a GCSE grade.

title: OS Map Skills: Unfamiliar Problem
concept: Map interpretation, transfer and limits of map evidence
enquiry: How can map evidence solve an unfamiliar problem?
current_ticket: Problem; grid/scale/relief evidence; solution; recommendation; adult owner/report-back.
elicited: A route/solution supported by mapped evidence, counter-route and limits.
interpret: Check method accuracy, use of scale/grid/relief, counter-route and what maps cannot settle.
bounded_voice: Give a keep/change/add term recommendation within the SoW decision-maker's power.
audience: Named SoW decision-maker receives evidence and gives reasoned response.
influence: Recommendation is acted on or declined with reasons; report-back to cohort.
next_step: Secure: new extract/constraints memo. Mixed: compare routes. Method: repair measurement. Access: enlarged/tactile/digital map.
tutor: Only subject-approved existing map evidence may be collated; no new calculation or recommendation is authored.
boundary: OS Education Licence/appropriate rights, source credit and no public unlicensed extract.
award: Exact UAS mapping; geography transfer is not automatic history award evidence.
